item.title: [6.8] CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes
item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

Recent advances in inference-time scaling have significantly improved the reasoning performance of large language models (LLMs). However, these methods typically rely on repeated generation or external verification. To address this limitation, we introduce CritICL, a novel inference-time framework that improves reasoning while maintaining high efficiency.

WHY IT MATTERS

CritICL introduces an interesting weak-to-strong inference-time approach by leveraging smaller model failure modes as structured guidance, though it remains an incremental research contribution.

item.description:

To support relighting and integration into standard rendering pipelines, the representation should include physically based rendering (PBR) modalities such as albedo, metallic-roughness, and surface normals. We propose Luce, a 3D representation that unifies geometry and PBR materials...

WHY IT MATTERS

Luce introduces a technically sound approach to single-image-to-3D generation by unifying geometry and PBR materials within a voxelized multimodal Gaussian cloud, achieving state-of-the-art results on Toys4K.

item.description:

Zero-shot cross-task generalization, where a policy must execute manipulation tasks never seen during training, remains a central challenge in robot learning. In large language models, a novel task can be performed simply by specifying it in the context, without any parameter update. This form of in-context learning (ICL) turns generalization into a problem of task specification.
